title: Pounds and Kilograms

sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of a kilogram as a bigger bag of sugar than a pound. One kilogram bag weighs the same as about 2.2 pound bags stacked together. So whenever you see 1 kg, picture it as 2.2 lb, the kilogram is always the heavier one.

### Question 2

Pounds are small bags and kilograms are big bags. If you have 11 small bags, you will end up with fewer big bags, so you split the 11 into groups worth 2.2 each. 11 divided by 2.2 makes 5 big bags, that is 5 kg.

### Question 3

Imagine a seesaw with 1 kilogram on one side. To balance it, you need to pile about 2.2 one-pound weights on the other side. Since it takes more than two pounds to match one kilogram, the kilogram is clearly the heavier unit.

### Question 4

You have 44 pound-sized scoops and want to know how many kilogram-sized scoops that fills. Each big scoop holds 2.2 little scoops, so you share the 44 into groups of 2.2. That gives 20 big scoops, 20 kg.

### Question 5

Dividing and multiplying pull in opposite directions. Since a kilogram is bigger than a pound, the kilogram number should be smaller. If you multiply instead, the number balloons the wrong way, turning a true 100 into a huge 484, nearly five times too big.

### Question 6

You cannot compare 3 big bags to 6 small bags just by the numbers. Turn the 3 big kilogram bags into small pound bags: each big bag is worth 2.2 small ones, so 3 becomes 6.6. Since 6.6 beats 6, the kilogram side wins.

### Question 7

The real number keeps going, 2.2046226..., like a ruler with tinier and tinier tick marks. So 2.2046 is already a trim of that number, and 2.2 is a shorter trim we use for fast head math. Knowing the digits keep going means you are not surprised when a scale reads a hair different.

### Question 8

Turning big kilogram bags into small pound bags always gives more bags. Each kilogram bag becomes 2.2 pound bags, so 30 bags become 30 times 2.2, which is 66 pound bags.

### Question 9

Turning big kilogram bags into small pound bags always gives more bags. Each kilogram bag becomes 2.2 pound bags, so 7.5 bags become 7.5 times 2.2, which is 16.5 pound bags.

### Question 10

Eighty-eight pound scoops poured into kilogram scoops make fewer scoops, because each big scoop swallows 2.2 little ones. Share 88 into groups of 2.2 and you get 40 big scoops, 40 kg.

### Question 11

A 3.5 kilogram baby sounds small, but pounds are little units so the number gets bigger. Each kilogram becomes 2.2 pounds, so 3.5 times 2.2 gives 7.7, a normal, healthy newborn weight you might hear announced at a birth.

### Question 12

You cannot say 50 beats 24 when they are measured in different-sized units. Change the 24 big kilogram scoops into little pound scoops: 24 times 2.2 is 52.8. Since 52.8 is more than 50, the kilogram child is actually the heavier one.
